key_insight: SqueezeBench turns math benchmarking into a moving target: every accepted solution must both prove a valid bound and strictly improve the current record, so progress cannot saturate.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical evaluation harness for theorem-proving systems that measures certified mathematical capability over time using machine-checked proofs rather than one-shot problem solving.
method: Each problem defines an integer function f(n) with known small-n values and maintains lower/upper certified records in Lean.
A submission must propose a new computable function, prove it bounds f, match or improve the current record everywhere, and beat it somewhere.
Two independent Lean kernels verify proofs, while maintainers only screen for exhaustive-search style cheating at larger n.
evidence_signal: The authors released 10 extremal-combinatorics problems with 20 initial records; frontier LLM agents achieved 82 accepted submissions, and newer models added 60 more and improved 19 of 20 records again.
watch_item: Because records can still lag the best published asymptotic bounds on most problems, the benchmark measures certified improvement under current records rather than full mathematical optimality.
paper_title: SqueezeBench: Saturation-Resilient Evaluation of Mathematical Capability
